what_to_include: You own your data and everything you put into or create in the tool: metadata, glossary, rules, results, lineage and configuration.
why_it_matters: Without it the assets you report under the policy, and their history, may not be yours to move.

what_to_include: Full export at any time, in named open formats, at no extra charge, tested before go-live and before each renewal.
why_it_matters: Keeps you able to report and to change product.

what_to_include: A costed exit plan in the contract, updated each year, with the supplier's help to move.
why_it_matters: An exit you have not planned is the legacy of the future.

what_to_include: A data processing schedule naming the processing, sub-processors and locations.
why_it_matters: Needed whenever personal data is processed for you.

what_to_include: A price for each capability, and the right to end one without ending the rest.
why_it_matters: Lets you replace one part without replacing everything.

what_to_include: A cap on price increases at renewal, and notice of any change.
why_it_matters: Keeps the cost in the business case true.

what_to_include: Security that matches the classification, notice of incidents within an agreed time, and help to respond.
why_it_matters: Critical data assets must stay available and protected.

what_to_include: The tool meets WCAG 2.2 AA for staff screens, with an accessibility statement kept up to date.
why_it_matters: The accessibility regulations apply to tools staff use.

what_to_include: Availability, recovery time and recovery point targets, reported each month, with remedies.
why_it_matters: Owners need to know how long a critical asset could be unavailable.

what_to_include: No use of your data to train models without written agreement, and a setting to turn AI features off.
why_it_matters: Keeps control of how your data is used.
